claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially exists as a high-temperature disordered BCC phase.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between the thermodynamic driving force for chemical ordering and kinetic limitations from sluggish atomic mobility.
At high temperatures, configurational entropy stabilizes the disordered BCC structure.
Cooling causes chemical short-range order to develop and lower the alloy's free energy through localized ordering.
The amount of ordering realized during cooling depends on whether atomic mobility and available time permit sufficient atomic rearrangement.
Chemical short-range order acts as a precursor to ordered clusters such as B2-type domains.
Slow cooling or intermediate isothermal holds enable more short-range order than rapid quenching.
Short-range ordering reduces local lattice distortions.
Evolution of short-range order triggers phase separation into ordered and disordered regions.
Rapid quenching kinetically traps a metastable, predominantly disordered BCC phase despite an underlying thermodynamic tendency to order.
Slowly cooled or isothermally held samples will exhibit diffraction or TEM signatures of emerging order.
Slowly cooled or isothermally held samples will eventually exhibit phase separation from the BCC matrix.
Rapidly quenched samples will retain a predominantly disordered BCC state.
Cooling-history-dependent microstructural differences will correlate with changes in mechanical properties.
Cooling-history-dependent microstructural differences may correlate with changes in transport properties.
The as-quenched baseline contains minimal short-range order because kinetic hindrance prevents ordering.
At sufficiently high temperatures diffusion is rapid enough for equilibrium to be reached immediately.
At sufficiently low temperatures slow diffusion is associated with the transformation already being complete.
Deformation or other processing routes can significantly alter diffusion rates and invalidate the proposed thermal-history mechanism.

contradictions.description: The mechanism associates low atomic mobility with kinetic trapping and suppression of transformation, whereas the boundary statement associates sufficiently slow diffusion at low temperature with transformation already being complete.
